title: Make your class AI ground-rules
goal: Make a one-page AI ground-rules sheet your class or staffroom will actually use.

blocks.title: One page beats a policy binder
blocks.body:
A 20-page policy nobody reads changes nothing. One clear page — on the staffroom wall, or shared with your class — changes how everyone uses AI.

Let's make yours in a few minutes. You decide what goes on it; AI just drafts the wording.

blocks.question: Which ground-rule is most useful on a shared one-pager?

options.text: "Keep students' names and personal details out of AI — de-identify first."

blocks.explanation: A rule people can actually follow beats one that's vague or fearful. 'Keep names out, de-identify first' tells a colleague exactly what to do on Monday morning — that's what makes a one-pager work.

blocks.scaffold: Draft a one-page AI ground-rules sheet for a {{gradeBand}} class. Cover three things in short, friendly points: privacy (no student names or personal details, de-identify first), honesty (say when AI helped), and always-check (a human checks facts, bias and local fit before using anything).

blocks.question: How usable is the ground-rules one-pager you just made — would you put it up this week?
